paidout.notes: Judgement: bank rule, not the payments formula. Nu is a deposit-funded lender: its operating cash flow is dominated by growth in credit-card receivables and loans (−12.90bn) and deposits (+5.91bn), not by collecting revenue, which is the condition that makes the formula meaningless for banks. So paidOut is null (comparable: false) and altPaidOut = noninterest expense − D&A − SBC + income taxes paid. Noninterest expense = transactional expenses (260,324) + total operating expenses (2,457,711), from the income statement; credit-loss allowance expenses (3,168,983) are a provision and interest and other financial expenses (2,834,859) are interest, both excluded as at BofA. D&A, SBC and taxes paid come from the cash-flow statement. Interest paid in cash (88,082) is far below interest expense (2,834,859); the cash-flow statement does not explain the gap, so it is recorded as stated. All figures US$ thousands. Reports in USD.
